title: 山行
author: Du Mu

translation: A slanting stone path climbs far up the cold mountain
Where white clouds are born, there are households
I stop my carriage, for I love the maple woods at dusk
Frost-covered leaves, redder than February flowers

annotations.寒山: cold mountain — the season is late autumn
annotations.斜: xié — slanting (older recitations read xiá for rhyme)
annotations.生处: where the clouds are born — a way of saying 'high up'
annotations.坐: here means 'because' — I stop *because* I love the view

appreciation: Du Mu overturns the autumn-is-sad cliché in four lines. Everyone else sees frost and thinks of death; he sees maple leaves redder than spring flowers. The poem is a lesson in attention: he literally stops his journey because a forest at dusk is worth being late for.
